about.text: Cream whipped until it is light and holds its shape: air bubbles are trapped in a foam stiffened by the cream's fat globules. It needs cream of roughly 30-40 % fat and about doubles in volume.

facts.v: 30–40 % (35–40 % set for whipping cream; 40 % whips easily, below 30 % whippability falls; about 25 % possible with added high-lecithin powder)
Fat globules collect on the walls of the air bubbles; some of their membranes are broken by the beating, and the free fat helps glue them together
Roughly handled or homogenised cream whips badly; overwhipping turns it to butter
The name slagroom is legally reserved for cow's milk cream with at least 30% fat
Served on the Åland pancake, hot or cold, with prune jam (raspberry for children)
